```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, message = FALSE)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

```{r meta}
mod_hr <- readModelDb("Minocha_2019_placebo_hr")
mod_qt <- readModelDb("Minocha_2019_placebo_QTcF")
mod_sbp <- readModelDb("Minocha_2019_placebo_sbp")
mod_dbp <- readModelDb("Minocha_2019_placebo_dbp")
```

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(mod_hr)$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.12640> (open access)
* Corrigendum: <https://doi.org/10.1111/cts.12773> (adds Table S1 with the
  between-subject variability estimates that were missing from Table 2, and a
  corrected Figure 2)

Minocha et al. pooled the placebo arms of 65 AbbVie phase I trials and fitted
four independent nonlinear mixed-effects models, one each for heart rate,
Fridericia-corrected QT interval (QTcF), systolic blood pressure (SBP) and
diastolic blood pressure (DBP). Every model has the same additive structure
(Eq. 2):

P_ij = BL_i + sum_k CIRC_k,ij +/- TE_ij + residual error

* **Baseline** `BL_i` is the value at midnight. Continuous covariates (age
  normalised to 30 years, weight to 70 kg) enter as a power function of the
  typical value, and sex and race as additive shifts with males and White
  subjects as the reference (Eq. 3). Between-subject variability on the
  baseline is additive.
* **Circadian rhythm** is a sum of cosines,
  `CIRC_k = AMP_k * cos(2 * 3.14 * (t - PS_k) / k)` with periods k of 24, 12 and
  6 h for heart rate and QTcF and a single 24-h cosine for SBP and DBP (Eq. 4).
  `PS_k` is the clock time (hours after midnight) at which that cosine peaks.
* **Time drift** `TE` is linear for heart rate (`0.15 * t / 24`, added) and an
  exponential approach to a plateau for the other three
  (`MAX * (1 - exp(-k * t / 24))`, subtracted).

`t` is clock time in hours since the midnight before the subject's first
recorded measurement, so `t = 35` is 11:00 am on the second study day. There is
no drug input: these are placebo backbones intended to be combined with a drug
effect.

```{r descriptions, results = "asis"}
for (m in list(mod_hr, mod_qt, mod_sbp, mod_dbp)) {
  cat("* ", rxode2::rxode(m)$description, "\n", sep = "")
}
```

# Population

Healthy volunteers who received placebo in single- and multiple-dose phase I
trials conducted by AbbVie between 2007 and 2014 (Minocha 2019 Table 1). Heart
rate and QTcF: 996 subjects from 63 studies, 16,509 observations (each the mean
of high-precision triplicate ECGs), from 3 days before the first placebo dose to
about 21 days after it. SBP and DBP: 1,035 subjects from 65 studies, 18,807
observations, from 3 days before to 12 weeks after the first placebo dose. The
cohorts were 75-76% male, 57% White, 33% Black, 8% Asian and 2% other race, with
mean (SD) age 34 (10) years and body weight 75 (12-13) kg.

The same information is available programmatically via each model's
`population` metadata:

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(mod_qt)$population)
```

# Source trace

Per-parameter origins are recorded as in-file comments next to every `ini()`
entry in `inst/modeldb/therapeuticArea/Minocha_2019_placebo_*.R`. "S1" is
Table S1 of the 2020 corrigendum.

| Element | Heart rate | QTcF | SBP | DBP | Source |
|---------|-----------|------|-----|-----|--------|
| Model structure | Eq. 9 | Eq. 10 | Eq. 11 | Eq. 12 | Eqs. 2-8; heart-rate code in Data S1 |
| `rbase` (male, White, 30 y, 70 kg) | 60.7 bpm | 400 ms | 123 mmHg | 78.3 mmHg | Table 2 |
| `e_sexf_rbase` | 6.8 | 14.7 | -8.3 | -4.7 | Table 2 |
| `e_race_black_rbase` | NS | -3.4 | 3.8 | 2.1 | Table 2 |
| `e_race_asian_rbase` | NS | NS | NS | -1.5 | Table 2 |
| `e_age_rbase` (power, /30 y) | NS | 0.031 | NS | 0.08 | Table 2 |
| `e_wt_rbase` (power, /70 kg) | NS | NS | 0.09 | NS | Table 2 |
| `amp_24h`, `acrophase_24h` | 2.2, 17.6 h | 2.6, 2.2 h | 1.0, 19.3 h | 1.6, 2.3 h | Table 2 |
| `amp_12h`, `acrophase_12h` | 0.5, 0 (held) | 2.0, 3.6 h | -- | -- | Table 2; Data S1 `PHI12 0 FIX` |
| `amp_6h`, `acrophase_6h` | 2.7, 2.8 h | 1.2, 1.7 h | -- | -- | Table 2 |
| Drift | `slope_drift` 0.15 /day | `drift_max` 5.0, k 1.4 /day | 7.6, 1.2 /day | 4.8, 1.6 /day | Table 2; Eqs. 5-6 |
| `etarbase` (variance) | 7.1^2 | 13.9^2 | 7.4^2 | 6.0^2 | Table 2 scaling factor, omega^2 = 1 |
| `etaamp_24h` | 3.52 | -- | 3.44 | 0.93 | S1 |
| `etaacrophase_24h` | 3.12 | 8.09 | -- | 6.12 | S1 |
| `etaamp_12h` | 1.27 | -- | -- | -- | S1 |
| `etaacrophase_12h` | -- | 2.24 | -- | -- | S1 |
| `etaacrophase_6h` | 0.638 | 0.967 | -- | -- | S1 |
| `etaslope_drift` | 0.204 | -- | -- | -- | S1 (Results: SD 0.45 bpm/day) |
| Residual error | `propSd` sqrt(0.004) | `addSd` 5.7 ms | 7.5 mmHg | 5.2 mmHg | Table 2 (footnote c: proportional for heart rate) |

NS: not significant, not in the final model; --: not part of that model.

# Typical-value time course (Figures 1 and 2)

Figures 1 and 2 show the typical prediction for a 30-year-old, 70-kg White male
between 24 and 72 h after the first midnight. The models carry no random effects
in this replication (`zeroRe(..., "omega")`); the plotted observation variables
are the model predictions without residual error. Figure 2 is the corrected
version printed in the 2020 corrigendum.

```{r typical}
typ_subject <- function(times, AGE = 30, WT = 70, SEXF = 0, RACE_BLACK = 0, RACE_ASIAN = 0) {
  data.frame(
    id = 1L, time = times, evid = 0L,
    AGE = AGE, WT = WT, SEXF = SEXF, RACE_BLACK = RACE_BLACK, RACE_ASIAN = RACE_ASIAN
  )
}
solve_typ <- function(mod, ev, dv) {
  sim <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod, "omega"), ev))
  data.frame(time = sim$time, value = sim[[dv]])
}

grid <- seq(24, 72, by = 0.1)
ev_ref <- typ_subject(grid)
typ <- bind_rows(
  solve_typ(mod_hr, ev_ref, "hr") |> mutate(variable = "Heart rate (beats/min)"),
  solve_typ(mod_qt, ev_ref, "QTcF") |> mutate(variable = "QTcF (ms)"),
  solve_typ(mod_sbp, ev_ref, "sbp") |> mutate(variable = "Systolic BP (mmHg)"),
  solve_typ(mod_dbp, ev_ref, "dbp") |> mutate(variable = "Diastolic BP (mmHg)")
)
```

```{r figure-1-2, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(typ, aes(time, value)) +
  geom_line(colour = "red") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(24, 48), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(24, 72, by = 6)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since midnight (h)", y = NULL,
    title = "Typical 30-year-old, 70-kg White male",
    caption = "Replicates the model lines of Figures 1a, 1b and corrected Figures 2a, 2b of Minocha 2019."
  )
```

The table below compares the packaged model with turning points read off the
published figure lines by the maintainers (reading precision about 0.3 units
for heart rate and blood pressure and 0.5 ms for QTcF).

```{r figure-1-2-check}
fig_read <- tibble::tribble(
  ~variable, ~dv, ~time, ~published,
  "Heart rate", "hr", 24, 58.5,
  "Heart rate", "hr", 30, 55.5,
  "Heart rate", "hr", 39, 65.3,
  "Heart rate", "hr", 54, 55.7,
  "Heart rate", "hr", 63, 65.5,
  "QTcF", "QTcF", 26, 400.3,
  "QTcF", "QTcF", 35, 390.5,
  "QTcF", "QTcF", 50, 399.5,
  "QTcF", "QTcF", 59, 390.0,
  "SBP", "sbp", 24, 118.0,
  "SBP", "sbp", 43, 117.2,
  "SBP", "sbp", 55, 114.9,
  "DBP", "dbp", 24, 75.9,
  "DBP", "dbp", 39, 72.3,
  "DBP", "dbp", 50, 75.3,
  "DBP", "dbp", 63, 72.0
)
mods <- list(hr = mod_hr, QTcF = mod_qt, sbp = mod_sbp, dbp = mod_dbp)
fig_read$simulated <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(fig_read)), function(i) {
  solve_typ(mods[[fig_read$dv[i]]], typ_subject(fig_read$time[i]), fig_read$dv[i])$value
}, numeric(1))
fig_read <- fig_read |> mutate(difference = simulated - published)

fig_read |>
  select(-dv) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Variable" = variable, "Time (h)" = time, "Figure" = published,
    "Model" = simulated, "Model - figure" = difference
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value model vs. values read from Figures 1 and 2 (corrected).")

# A transcription error in an amplitude, phase or drift parameter moves these
# points by several units; the bounds sit outside the reading precision plus the
# constant ~0.8 ms QTcF offset described under Assumptions and deviations.
tol <- c(hr = 1, QTcF = 1.5, sbp = 0.75, dbp = 0.75)
stopifnot(all(abs(fig_read$difference) < tol[fig_read$dv]))
```

## Peak and trough clock times

The Results ('Effect of circadian rhythm') state the clock times of the peaks
and troughs and the peak-to-trough differences of the typical profile. These are
checked on the third study day (48-72 h), where the drift has almost reached its
plateau.

```{r peaks}
day3 <- typ |> filter(time >= 48, time <= 72)
peaks <- day3 |>
  group_by(variable) |>
  summarise(
    peak_clock = time[which.max(value)] - 48,
    trough_clock = time[which.min(value)] - 48,
    peak_to_trough = max(value) - min(value),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
published_peaks <- tibble::tribble(
  ~variable, ~peak_pub, ~trough_pub, ~diff_pub,
  "Heart rate (beats/min)", 15, 6, 10,
  "QTcF (ms)", 2, 11, 10,
  "Systolic BP (mmHg)", 19, 8, 2,
  "Diastolic BP (mmHg)", 2, 14, 3.5
)
peak_cmp <- left_join(peaks, published_peaks, by = "variable")
peak_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Variable" = variable,
    "Peak clock time, model (h)" = peak_clock, "Peak, paper (h)" = peak_pub,
    "Trough clock time, model (h)" = trough_clock, "Trough, paper (h)" = trough_pub,
    "Peak - trough, model" = peak_to_trough, "Peak - trough, paper (approx.)" = diff_pub
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Circadian turning points of the typical profile on day 3.")

# The paper rounds clock times to the hour and differences to 'approximately'.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(peak_cmp$peak_clock - peak_cmp$peak_pub) <= 1),
  all(abs(peak_cmp$trough_clock - peak_cmp$trough_pub) <= 1),
  all(abs(peak_cmp$peak_to_trough - peak_cmp$diff_pub) < 0.5)
)
```

The Results also give the drift half-lives: about 12 h (QTcF), 14 h (SBP) and
10 h (DBP).

```{r drift-half-lives}
half_life_h <- log(2) / exp(c(
  QTcF = rxode2::rxode(mod_qt)$theta[["lkdrift"]],
  SBP = rxode2::rxode(mod_sbp)$theta[["lkdrift"]],
  DBP = rxode2::rxode(mod_dbp)$theta[["lkdrift"]]
)) * 24
round(half_life_h, 1)
stopifnot(all(abs(half_life_h - c(12, 14, 10)) < 0.6))
```

# Effect of sex and race at 11:00 am (Figure 3)

Figure 3 shows model-predicted values at 11:00 am for 1,000 subjects in each of
four groups (White or Black, male or female; 30 years, 70 kg). Here 200 subjects
per group are simulated with between-subject variability at `t = 35` h (11:00 am
on study day 2). The observation columns returned by `rxSolve()` are individual
predictions without residual error.

```{r figure-3-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2019)
groups <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group, ~SEXF, ~RACE_BLACK,
  "White-Male", 0, 0,
  "Black-Male", 0, 1,
  "White-Female", 1, 0,
  "Black-Female", 1, 1
)
n_per_group <- 200
ev_fig3 <- groups |>
  mutate(g = row_number()) |>
  tidyr::uncount(n_per_group, .id = "k") |>
  mutate(
    id = (g - 1L) * n_per_group + k, time = 35, evid = 0L,
    AGE = 30, WT = 70, RACE_ASIAN = 0
  ) |>
  select(id, time, evid, AGE, WT, SEXF, RACE_BLACK, RACE_ASIAN, group)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(ev_fig3$id))

sim_one <- function(mod, dv, label) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_fig3, keep = "group")) |>
    transmute(group, variable = label, value = .data[[dv]])
}
fig3 <- bind_rows(
  sim_one(mod_hr, "hr", "Heart rate (beats/min)"),
  sim_one(mod_qt, "QTcF", "QTcF (ms)"),
  sim_one(mod_sbp, "sbp", "Systolic BP (mmHg)"),
  sim_one(mod_dbp, "dbp", "Diastolic BP (mmHg)")
) |>
  mutate(group = factor(group, levels = groups$group))
```

```{r figure-3, fig.height = 6}
ggplot(fig3, aes(group, value, fill = group)) +
  geom_boxplot(show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    x = NULL, y = "Value at 11:00 am",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 3 of Minocha 2019 (200 simulated subjects per group)."
  ) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

The medians and interquartile ranges in Figure 3 were read by the maintainers
(reading precision about 1 unit).

```{r figure-3-check}
fig3_pub <- tibble::tribble(
  ~variable, ~group, ~median_pub, ~q25_pub, ~q75_pub,
  "Heart rate (beats/min)", "White-Male", 59, 54.5, 64.5,
  "Heart rate (beats/min)", "Black-Male", 59, 54, 64.5,
  "Heart rate (beats/min)", "White-Female", 66.5, 61.5, 72,
  "Heart rate (beats/min)", "Black-Female", 66.5, 61.5, 72,
  "QTcF (ms)", "White-Male", 392, 383, 402,
  "QTcF (ms)", "Black-Male", 388, 380, 398,
  "QTcF (ms)", "White-Female", 407, 397, 418,
  "QTcF (ms)", "Black-Female", 404, 394, 413,
  "Systolic BP (mmHg)", "White-Male", 116, 110.5, 121,
  "Systolic BP (mmHg)", "Black-Male", 119.5, 115, 124.5,
  "Systolic BP (mmHg)", "White-Female", 108, 102.5, 113,
  "Systolic BP (mmHg)", "Black-Female", 111, 106.5, 116.5,
  "Diastolic BP (mmHg)", "White-Male", 73.5, 69, 77.5,
  "Diastolic BP (mmHg)", "Black-Male", 75.5, 71, 79.5,
  "Diastolic BP (mmHg)", "White-Female", 68, 64, 72.5,
  "Diastolic BP (mmHg)", "Black-Female", 70.5, 66.5, 74.5
)
dv_of <- c(
  "Heart rate (beats/min)" = "hr", "QTcF (ms)" = "QTcF",
  "Systolic BP (mmHg)" = "sbp", "Diastolic BP (mmHg)" = "dbp"
)
fig3_pub$typical <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(fig3_pub)), function(i) {
  g <- groups[groups$group == fig3_pub$group[i], ]
  dv <- dv_of[[fig3_pub$variable[i]]]
  solve_typ(mods[[dv]], typ_subject(35, SEXF = g$SEXF, RACE_BLACK = g$RACE_BLACK), dv)$value
}, numeric(1))
fig3_sim <- fig3 |>
  group_by(variable, group) |>
  summarise(
    median_sim = median(value),
    iqr_sim = IQR(value),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(group = as.character(group))
fig3_cmp <- left_join(fig3_pub, fig3_sim, by = c("variable", "group")) |>
  mutate(iqr_pub = q75_pub - q25_pub)

fig3_cmp |>
  select(variable, group, median_pub, typical, median_sim, iqr_pub, iqr_sim) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Variable" = variable, "Group" = group,
    "Median, Figure 3" = median_pub, "Typical value" = typical,
    "Median, simulated" = median_sim,
    "IQR, Figure 3" = iqr_pub, "IQR, simulated" = iqr_sim
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Figure 3 medians and interquartile ranges vs. the model.")

# 1. Deterministic: the typical value of each group against the figure median.
#    The sex and race shifts separate the groups by 2-15 units; the bound is the
#    reading precision plus the ~0.8 ms QTcF offset noted under Assumptions.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig3_cmp$typical - fig3_cmp$median_pub) < 2))

# 2. Stochastic: the 200-subject median sits on the typical value. The sampling
#    SD of that median is about 1.25 x SD / sqrt(200) = 0.089 x the baseline SD
#    (0.6 bpm, 1.2 ms, 0.7 and 0.5 mmHg), so 0.45 x the baseline SD is about
#    5 sampling SDs: it fails only for a real error in the variability model.
bl_sd <- c(
  "Heart rate (beats/min)" = 7.1, "QTcF (ms)" = 13.9,
  "Systolic BP (mmHg)" = 7.4, "Diastolic BP (mmHg)" = 6.0
)
stopifnot(all(
  abs(fig3_cmp$median_sim - fig3_cmp$typical) < 0.45 * bl_sd[fig3_cmp$variable]
))

# 3. Spread: interquartile range pooled over the four groups (800 subjects,
#    sampling SD about 4%) against the mean of the four published IQRs.
#    Adding the residual error would widen the SBP IQR by about 40%.
iqr_pooled <- fig3 |>
  left_join(fig3_cmp |> select(variable, group, typical), by = c("variable", "group")) |>
  group_by(variable) |>
  summarise(iqr_sim = IQR(value - typical), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(
    fig3_cmp |> group_by(variable) |> summarise(iqr_pub = mean(iqr_pub), .groups = "drop"),
    by = "variable"
  )
iqr_pooled
stopifnot(all(abs(iqr_pooled$iqr_sim / iqr_pooled$iqr_pub - 1) < 0.2))
```

# Effect of age and body weight (Figure 4)

Figure 4 shows the median and 90% prediction interval of QTcF and DBP for White
males aged 18, 30 or 60 years (70 kg), and of SBP for White males weighing 40,
70 or 120 kg (30 years). 200 subjects per stratum are simulated here.

```{r figure-4-sim}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2020)
grid4 <- seq(24, 72, by = 1)
make_stratum <- function(n, stratum, AGE, WT, id_offset) {
  tidyr::expand_grid(id = id_offset + seq_len(n), time = grid4) |>
    mutate(
      evid = 0L, AGE = AGE, WT = WT, SEXF = 0, RACE_BLACK = 0, RACE_ASIAN = 0,
      stratum = stratum
    )
}
ev_age <- bind_rows(
  make_stratum(200, "18 years", 18, 70, 0L),
  make_stratum(200, "30 years", 30, 70, 200L),
  make_stratum(200, "60 years", 60, 70, 400L)
)
ev_wt <- bind_rows(
  make_stratum(200, "40 kg", 30, 40, 0L),
  make_stratum(200, "70 kg", 30, 70, 200L),
  make_stratum(200, "120 kg", 30, 120, 400L)
)
stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(ev_age[, c("id", "time")]),
  !anyDuplicated(ev_wt[, c("id", "time")])
)

summ <- function(mod, ev, dv, label) {
  as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, keep = "stratum")) |>
    group_by(stratum, time) |>
    summarise(
      Q05 = quantile(.data[[dv]], 0.05), Q50 = median(.data[[dv]]),
      Q95 = quantile(.data[[dv]], 0.95), .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(variable = label)
}
fig4 <- bind_rows(
  summ(mod_qt, ev_age, "QTcF", "QTcF (ms)"),
  summ(mod_dbp, ev_age, "dbp", "Diastolic BP (mmHg)"),
  summ(mod_sbp, ev_wt, "sbp", "Systolic BP (mmHg)")
) |>
  mutate(stratum = factor(stratum, levels = c(
    "18 years", "30 years", "60 years", "40 kg", "70 kg", "120 kg"
  )))
```

```{r figure-4, fig.height = 7}
ggplot(fig4, aes(time, Q50, colour = stratum, fill = stratum)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = Q05, ymax = Q95), alpha = 0.15, colour = NA) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_grid(variable ~ stratum, scales = "free") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(24, 72, by = 12)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time since midnight (h)", y = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Minocha 2019 (median and 90% prediction interval, 200 subjects per stratum)."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

The typical profile at `t = 24` h (midnight starting day 2) read from Figure 4
is compared with the typical-value model below.

```{r figure-4-check}
fig4_pub <- tibble::tribble(

  "QTcF (ms)", "QTcF", "18 years", 18, 70, 391.5,
  "QTcF (ms)", "QTcF", "30 years", 30, 70, 397.5,
  "QTcF (ms)", "QTcF", "60 years", 60, 70, 406.5,
  "Diastolic BP (mmHg)", "dbp", "18 years", 18, 70, 72.2,
  "Diastolic BP (mmHg)", "dbp", "30 years", 30, 70, 75.5,
  "Diastolic BP (mmHg)", "dbp", "60 years", 60, 70, 80.1,
  "Systolic BP (mmHg)", "sbp", "40 kg", 30, 40, 111.5,
  "Systolic BP (mmHg)", "sbp", "70 kg", 30, 70, 117.3,
  "Systolic BP (mmHg)", "sbp", "120 kg", 30, 120, 123.2
)
fig4_pub$simulated <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(fig4_pub)), function(i) {
  solve_typ(
    mods[[fig4_pub$dv[i]]],
    typ_subject(24, AGE = fig4_pub$AGE[i], WT = fig4_pub$WT[i]),
    fig4_pub$dv[i]
  )$value
}, numeric(1))
fig4_pub |>
  select(variable, stratum, published, simulated) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Variable" = variable, "Stratum" = stratum,
    "Figure 4 at 24 h" = published, "Typical-value model" = simulated
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Figure 4 median at 24 h vs. typical-value model.")

# The age and weight power exponents shift these values by 4-9 units between
# strata; the bound is the reading precision of the small Figure 4 panels.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig4_pub$simulated - fig4_pub$published) < 1.5))
```

# Why there is no NCA

These are placebo models with no drug input, so there is no concentration
profile to summarise with PKNCA. The checks above use the quantities the paper
reports instead: typical-value profiles (Figures 1, 2 and 4), circadian peak and
trough clock times, drift half-lives, and covariate-stratified distributions
(Figure 3).

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Corrigendum.** Table 2 of the original article omitted the between-subject
  variances of the amplitudes, phase shifts and the heart-rate drift slope. They
  are taken from Table S1 of the 2020 corrigendum
  (doi:10.1111/cts.12773). The heart-rate drift-slope variance there (0.204)
  agrees with the SD of 0.45 bpm/day quoted in the original Results. The
  corrigendum also replaced Figure 2 because the code that drew it shifted the
  curves by a constant; the checks above use the corrected Figure 2.
* **Baseline variability parameterisation.** The authors estimated each
  baseline eta as `ETA * THETA` with the eta variance held at 1, so that THETA
  is the between-subject SD. The packaged models use the equivalent single
  eta with variance THETA^2 (for example 7.1^2 = 50.41 for heart rate).
  Likewise, the additive residual SDs (`addSd`) are the published scaling
  factors with sigma^2 = 1.
* **Heart-rate residual error.** Table 2 lists 0.004 in the row labelled
  'sigma^2 (additive residual error)' for heart rate, with footnote c stating
  that heart rate uses a proportional error. The authors' control stream (Data
  S1) confirms a purely proportional error, so `propSd = sqrt(0.004) = 0.0632`.
* **Heart-rate 12-h phase shift.** Table 2 lists it as 'NS'; the Results explain
  that it was not estimated because the estimate was close to 12 h, and Data S1
  holds `PHI12` at 0. With a 12-h period a phase of 0 and of 12 h are the same,
  so `acrophase_12h` is held at 0.
* **The constant 3.14.** Eq. 4 and the authors' control stream both use
  `2 * 3.14` rather than `2 * pi`; the packaged models keep 3.14 because that is
  the form that was fitted. Over three weeks the difference shifts the cosines
  by about 0.25 h.
* **Time origin.** The authors' `TIME` is continuous clock time from the
  midnight before each subject's first record, which includes screening (about
  3 days before the first placebo dose); the drift terms are anchored there too.
  Users simulating a trial should set `t = 0` at the midnight before the first
  measurement, not at the first dose. For crossover studies the authors reset
  each period with `EVID = 4`.
* **Covariate reference groups.** Males and White subjects are the reference
  categories (the most frequent ones). Race groups whose shift was not
  significant (Asian for heart rate, QTcF and SBP; other race for all four)
  share the White baseline. Screened but not retained covariates are listed in
  each model's `covariatesDataExcluded`.
* **DBP age-exponent interval.** Table 2 prints the bootstrap interval of the
  DBP age exponent as (0.07, 1.0); the upper bound is presumably 0.10. The
  point estimate 0.08 is used.
* **QTcF offset in Figure 1b.** The typical QTcF from the published parameters
  sits about 0.8 ms above the Figure 1b line at every turning point read, while
  heart rate (Figure 1a) and the corrected blood-pressure lines (Figure 2) agree
  within reading precision. A constant offset of this size (0.2%) is consistent
  with rounding of the published estimates or with how the figure line was
  drawn; the parameters are used as published.
* **Figure 3 and 4 cohorts.** The simulations use 200 subjects per group rather
  than the paper's 1,000, and Figure 3 is evaluated on study day 2 (`t = 35` h)
  because the paper does not say which day was used. The simulated values are
  individual predictions without residual error. Their interquartile ranges
  are 4-7% narrower than those read from Figure 3; adding the residual error
  would widen the SBP range by about 40%, far beyond the figure, so the figure
  is taken to show predictions without residual error.
